content: PDF pipelines: pandoc lang metadata (BCP 47, e.g. pt-BR) drives localization of the document itself in LaTeX/ConTeXt PDF output: babel (pdfLaTeX) or polyglossia (XeLaTeX/LuaLaTeX) load language hyphenation patterns and translate fixed element names (Chapter -> Kapitel, Table of Contents -> Inhaltsverzeichnis) and localize dates; otherlangs adds secondary languages; lang-dir/dir handle direction; non-Latin scripts may need per-language fonts (babelfonts). Quarto (pandoc-based) documents the same behavior. WeasyPrint (non-LaTeX engine) hyphenates via CSS hyphens and the document lang attribute using pyphen dictionaries - language must be declared for correct hyphenation. Implication: setting lang on generated PDF sources is a one-line change with concrete typographic effects, engine-dependent.
